prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), the visible actions and interactions, and the setting; remain concrete, image‑centered and avoid speculation, inference or subjective judgment. Use camera‑relative language (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right; facing the camera/in profile/back to the camera). For every visible person or object state whether it is stationary or moving; for every moving subject give horizontal direction first then vertical relative to the image frame (for example, "from left to right," "toward the camera while ascending"), name any visible phase of motion (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing) and indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential. For each moving subject describe trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to her right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward/away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame). For people, explicitly note whether they are alone or in a group and give counts and proximity (walking alone, two people together, a cluster of three closely spaced). For gestures and hand/object interactions specify direction and type (pointing with an extended right arm, gesturing outward with an open palm), which hand/side is used, whether the hand is in contact, gripping, resting, or merely near an object, and whether it is moving or still. For head orientation and gaze give clear phrases for every visible person (for example, "head turned slightly left, gaze down at a phone," "looking directly at the camera," "eyes directed up and to the right"). Describe body posture with concrete camera‑relative terms (standing, weight on left leg, slightly leaning forward, seated, crouching, mid‑jump) and clarify orientation to the camera. For animals describe direction and, only when the gait is clearly visible, name the gait (walking/trotting/running/cantering); if gait is not clear, describe visible leg positions or alternating leg motion rather than guessing. When subjects interact, report only observable cues and roles using visual evidence (open mouth facing another as an indicator of speaking; turned body, raised hand or pointing as addressing; facing and still as listening). Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and scale (directly in front of, a few feet/meters apart, in a line, scattered). Optionally note lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues. Keep the caption factual, tightly worded, and output exactly one single sentence.
